statements.impact_statement: The vulnerable module golang.org/x/crypto is declared at v0.31.0, which is inside the affected range (all versions before v0.52.0). The flaw is in the golang.org/x/crypto/ssh package: a malicious SSH peer sends unsolicited global request responses, which blocks the connection read loop and leaks a goroutine per connection. No first-party Go file imports golang.org/x/crypto/ssh. The only x/crypto packages headscale imports are acme, acme/autocert and bcrypt, none of which touch the ssh package. The one transitive route I found is tailscale.com/tsnet, imported in hscontrol/tailsql.go. Its SSH code uses the fork github.com/tailscale/golang-x-crypto/ssh, which go.mod lists as indirect, not golang.org/x/crypto/ssh. I checked this for ipn/ipnlocal/ssh.go in tailscale v1.78.0, not v1.79.0-pre, and I did not read the Go module cache, so the claim covers that one file only. Headscale also has no

CVE-2026-39832 (GO-2026-5006 / GHSA-f5wc-c3c7-36mc) affects golang.org/x/crypto before 0.52.0. The flaw is in the ssh/agent package: client.Add and keyring.Add drop constraint extensions such as restrict-destination-v00@openssh.com, and NewKeyring() silently ignores unsupported ones. This repository pins golang.org/x/crypto v0.31.0, so the module is present and in the affected range. First-party Go code imports only three x/crypto packages: acme, acme/autocert and bcrypt. It never imports golang.org/x/crypto/ssh or ssh/agent, and it never calls NewKeyring or the agent client. The only 'ssh' matches in hscontrol are Tailscale SSH ACL policy types, which are unrelated to x/crypto. No vendored copy exists. Headscale is a control server and has no SSH agent forwarding feature. Limitation: I could not read the Go module cache, so I could not confirm that a transitive dependency such as tailsc

github.com/jackc/pgx/v5 v5.7.1 is in the affected range (<5.9.0; fixed in 5.9.0), so the package is present. The Go vulnerability database entry GO-2026-4771 lists the vulnerable symbols as pgproto3 Backend.Receive and Bind.Decode. In pgx v5.7.1, pgproto3.Backend is the server side of the PostgreSQL wire protocol. Its Receive method parses messages sent by a client (Bind, Parse, Query and so on). Headscale only reaches pgx as a PostgreSQL client, through gorm.io/driver/postgres, and that client uses pgproto3.Frontend. Frontend.Receive decodes server messages (BindComplete, DataRow and so on) and never references Bind or Backend.Receive. The repository has no first-party Go code that imports pgx or pgproto3, builds a pgproto3 Backend, or acts as a PostgreSQL server or proxy. So no execution path reaches Backend.Receive or Bind.Decode. The advisory text is thin and gives no root-cause deta

Versions before 0.52.0 are affected. go.mod and go.sum resolve golang.org/x/crypto to v0.31.0, which is inside the range, so the package is present and affected.

No first-party Go file imports golang.org/x/crypto/ssh. The searches found zero imports and zero calls to Dial, NewClientConn, NewServerConn or the Session methods. Headscale uses crypto only through other subpackages. The only plausible transitive route is tailscale.com/tsnet, which hscontrol/tailsql.go imports. That code runs only when HEADSCALE_DEBUG_TAILSQL_ENABLED is set. I could not read the module cache, so I checked the upstream Tailscale source instead, and it points the other way. The vulnerable symbols are Backend.Receive and FunctionCall.Decode. Headscale only uses pgx as a database client through gorm.Open(postgres.Open(...)). The client path uses pgproto3.Frontend, which does not call Backend.Receive. The advisory (GO-2026-5023 / GHSA-x527-x647-q7gg) affects golang.org/x/crypto/ssh before v0.52.0. It is a server-side bug. When an ssh.ServerConfig uses a callback other than the public-key callback, source-address validation is skipped. Only server code that calls ssh.NewServerConn is exposed. This repository requires golang.org/x/crypto v0.31.0, which is in the affected range. However, no Go source file in the tree imports golang.org/x/crypto/ssh. The only x/crypto imports are acme, acme/autocert and bcrypt. No file references NewServerConn, ssh.ServerConfig or VerifiedPublicKeyCallback, and there is no vendor directory. The 'ssh' hits in the tree are ACL policy JSON fields and integration tests that shell out to /usr/bin/ssh. Headscale runs no SSH server. The Tailscale SSH server code that headscale's dependency tree could bring in uses a separate fork module, github.com/tailscale/gol

The advisory (CVE-2026-39831, GHSA-89gr-r52h-f8rx, GO-2026-5019) covers golang.org/x/crypto/ssh, v0.1.0 to before v0.52.0. Verify() for the FIDO/U2F key types sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com and sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com does not check the User Presence flag. This repository resolves golang.org/x/crypto to v0.31.0, which is inside the affected range, so the package is present. No first-party Go file imports golang.org/x/crypto/ssh. The only x/crypto subpackages imported are bcrypt (hscontrol/db/api_key.go) and acme and acme/autocert (hscontrol/app.go), none of which touch the SSH code. The repo has no SSH server, no ssh.ServerConfig, no PublicKeyCallback, no tailssh, and no sk-* key handling. Verify() on those key types only runs when an SSH server authenticates a client's public-key signature, so no path from headscale's network surfaces reaches it. Limitation: hscontrol/tailsql.go

There is no vendor directory. headscale is a Tailscale control server and does not act as an SSH agent. The Tailscale SSH code in tailscale.com uses the separate fork module github.com/tailscale/golang-x-crypto, not this module's ssh/agent. The advisory's affected range is runc <=1.2.7, <=1.3.2 and <=1.4.0-rc.2. The fixes are in 1.2.8, 1.3.3 and 1.4.0-rc.3. This repository (headscale) resolves github.com/opencontainers/runc v1.2.3 as an indirect dependency in go.mod and go.sum, so the version is in the affected range. However, no Go source file imports any runc package. The vulnerable code is in runc's libcontainer, which runs when runc starts a container, not when a library is linked. A search found no references to libcontainer or maskPaths. The only mention of runc outside go.mod and go.sum is a comment URL in integration/dockertestutil/config.go. This repository pins golang.org/x/crypto v0.31.0, so the version is in range. The vulnerable package is not used, though. The advisory (GHSA-78h2-9frx-2jm8 / GO-2026-4945) covers a panic in go-jose JWE decryption. cipher.KeyUnwrap() panics when a JWE uses a key-wrapping alg (*KW, excluding AxxxGCMKW) and has an empty encrypted_key. It is reached through ParseEncrypted*/Decrypt. Affected ranges are v3 3.0.0-3.0.4 (fixed 3.0.5) and v4 4.0.0-4.1.3 (fixed 4.1.4). This repo resolves go-jose/v3 v3.0.3 and go-jose/v4 v4.0.2, both in the affected ranges, but only as indirect dependencies. No first-party Go file imports go-jose. The only plausible route is github.com/coreos/go-oidc/v3 v3.11.0, which hscontrol/oidc.go imports to verify ID tokens. According to the upstream v3.11.0 source (fetched from GitHub, not read from a local module cache), go-oidc only calls jose.ParseSigned in verify.go and jwks.go. It never calls ParseEncrypted or Decrypt, so the JWE/KeyUnwrap path is not reached. I did not inspect the source

go-jose is present only as an indirect dependency, at v3.0.3 and v4.0.2. Both are inside the affected ranges (v3 3.0.0-3.0.4, v4 4.0.0-4.1.3). No first-party Go file imports go-jose or calls any JWE API. The only route to go-jose is github.com/coreos/go-oidc/v3 v3.11.0, called from hscontrol/oidc.go. Its IDTokenVerifier.Verify and RemoteKeySet only use jose.ParseSigned, JSONWebSignature.Verify and JSONWebKeySet, which are the JWS path and never reach JWE decryption or KeyUnwrap. I checked go-oidc against upstream source fetched from GitHub, because the module cache is outside the sandbox, so that part is not mechanically checkable inside the repository. statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-63209 (GHSA-259r-337f-4rfw, GO-2026-5841) is an integer overflow in github.com/klauspost/compress/s2. s2.NewDict() accepts a crafted dictionary, and Dict.Encode() then reads out of bounds, which crashes the process. It affects v1.0 through v1.18.6 and is fixed in v1.18.7. This repo resolves v1.17.11, which is inside the affected range, so the module is present. The only first-party use is the zstd subpackage (hscontrol/mapper/mapper.go), which is a different package from s2. The advisory names only s2. No first-party Go file imports s2 or calls NewDict or MakeDict, and there is no vendor directory. The zstd encoder.go at v1.17.11 does not import s2. Exploitation also needs an application that passes attacker-supplied dictionary data to s2.NewDict(). Headscale's only compression use is encoding its own map responses with zstd, with no dictionary input. Limitation: I could not rea

CVE-2026-41567 is a Moby/Docker Engine daemon bug. In the daemon's handling of PUT /containers/{id}/archive (docker cp -), a compressed (xz/gzip) upload makes the daemon look up the decompressor (xz, unpigz) in the container's filesystem instead of the host's. A trojanized image can then run code as the daemon. The advisory lists Docker Engine before 29.5.1 and moby/moby v2 before v2.0.0-beta.14 as affected, and does not name specific functions.
This repo's go.mod pins github.com/docker/docker v27.4.0+incompatible as an indirect dependency. That version is inside the affected range, so the module is present. No first-party Go file imports github.com/docker/docker or any of its daemon, api, client or pkg packages (0 hits). The vulnerable code is the daemon's server-side archive handler. It never runs in headscale or its tests, because the daemon is a separate external process.

The affected range is Docker Engine before 29.5.1, Docker Daemon 28.5.2 and earlier, and Moby daemon before 2.0.0-beta.14. statements.impact_statement: GO-2025-3787 (GHSA-fv92-fjc5-jj9h, no CVE) affects github.com/go-viper/mapstructure/v2 before v2.3.0. When a decode fails (WeakDecode and the decode helpers behind it), the error text includes the raw input value, which can leak sensitive data into logs or responses. This repo resolves the module to v2.2.1 as an indirect dependency of spf13/viper v1.20.0-alpha.6, so the version is in range. The only decode path is viper.UnmarshalKey("dns.extra_records", &extraRecords) in hscontrol/types/config.go. It runs once at startup, on operator-authored config (file or HEADSCALE_ env vars), and decodes into []tailcfg.DNSRecord (DNS names and IPs, not secrets). The error is wrapped and returned from config loading, not sent to a network client. The other viper calls are GetString/GetBool/GetStringSlice and similar, which use cast and not mapstructure struct decoding. The repo has no direct mapstruct

GO-2026-6237 affects github.com/insomniacslk/dhcp/dhcpv4/nclient4, specifically BroadcastRawUDPConn.ReadFrom. A short IPv4 payload makes the computed DHCP length negative, which panics. All versions before v0.0.0-20260719225207-c76316d4aa82 are affected. The repo resolves the module to v0.0.0-20240129002554-15c9b8791914, so the version is in range. It is only an indirect dependency (go.mod, `// indirect`), and there is no vendor directory. No first-party Go source imports insomniacslk/dhcp or nclient4, and nothing references BroadcastRawUDPConn. The only transitive route is through tailscale.com v1.79.0-pre and similar. pkg.go.dev's imported-by list for nclient4 shows no tailscale.com package, so the vulnerable package should not be compiled into headscale. Caveat: I could not read the Go module cache, and the pkg.go.dev result was a condensed summary rather than a verbatim list. The no-

GO-2026-5932 covers only the deprecated golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp packages (openpgp, packet, armor, clearsign, errors, elgamal, s2k). It lists all versions as affected and no fix, with no CVE alias. The repo declares golang.org/x/crypto v0.31.0, so the module is present and in range. But the vulnerable packages are separate subpackages, and no first-party Go source imports them. The only x/crypto imports are acme, acme/autocert and bcrypt, which are different packages. The string 'openpgp' appears nowhere in the tree, and there is no vendor directory. Caveat: I could not inspect the Go module cache, so I could not check mechanically whether a dependency such as tailscale.com imports x/crypto/openpgp. go.sum has no OpenPGP-related modules such as ProtonMail/go-crypto, keybase or gopenpgp, which is consistent with no OpenPGP use. This is a moderate-confidence call and is worth confirming
